grammar.title: The Subjunctive (I insist that he be)
grammar.explanation:
The subjunctive expresses demands, suggestions, and necessities. It uses the base form of the verb, whatever the subject is.

After verbs like **insist**, **demand**, **suggest**, and **recommend**, use **that** + subject + base verb.

The verb never changes for the subject. We say **I insist that he be** on time, not "he is" on time.

The subjunctive also appears after adjectives like **essential**, **vital**, and **crucial**.

In formal style, **were** replaces **was** in unreal conditionals: **If I were** you, I would choose the simpler outfit.
examples: *The designer insisted that the gown be* finished by Friday. (demand)
*She suggested that he wear* a more understated ensemble to the interview. (suggestion)
*It is essential that the fabric drape* perfectly on the runway. (necessity)
*The director demanded that the couture show start* exactly on time. (demand)
*If I were* the stylist, I would choose a dapper suit with a flamboyant scarf. (unreal conditional)
*The fashion house recommends that every bespoke suit be* fitted twice before delivery. (recommendation)
